assertions.text: List values in the table use bracket syntax like [tech:java, biz:sales, dev:ci] — not comma-separated strings without brackets.
Empty list input uses [] (not a blank cell, which represents null). The distinction between empty list and null is preserved.
assertions.evidence: Empty tags list | [] | tech | [] and No tags match category | ... | business | []

assertions.text: Values containing pipes (|), brackets, or colons (:) are properly quoted (e.g. "tech:java") so they don't conflict with table syntax.
assertions.evidence: ["tech:java", "dev:kotlin", "biz:sales", "ops:deploy"] — all colon-containing values are quoted strings

assertions.text: Set<String> values in the table use curly brace syntax like {tech, dev} — not bracket syntax [tech, dev] which is for lists.
assertions.evidence: Optional adds one extra prefix | ... | tech | {biz} | ... and Optional adds multiple prefixes | ... | {biz, ops} |

assertions.text: Cell values containing newlines use \n escaping — not literal line breaks that would break the table row structure.
Values containing pipe characters (|) are quoted so they don't conflict with the markdown table column separator.
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Filtered tags?' or 'Result?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 3 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit:1.2.1 as a test dependency
The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
